candidate_evidence.quote: [DRUG] Cancer Therapeutic Procedure (other names: anticancer therapy, Cancer Therapy, Cancer Treatment, Malignant Neoplasm Therapy, Malignant Neoplasm Treatment): Receive in-home standard of care cancer-treatment
Participant must be receiving a standard-of-care treatment regimen listed in this protocol that is being used in accordance with standard medical practice.
Receiving any investigational agent which would be considered as a treatment for the primary neoplasm.

role_evidence.quote: Patients receive in-home standard of care cancer-treatment through CCBW according to standard clinical practice for up to 12 weeks in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
Patients who, according to documentation from their treating provider, plan to continue the eligible treatment regimen they are currently prescribed for \>= 12 weeks from the time of registration

agents.drug_class_hint: patient's ongoing standard-of-care regimen from a protocol list (e.g. checkpoint inhibitors, bevacizumab, bortezomib, hormonal agents); the trial tests in-home vs clinic delivery location
arms: Health services research (CCBW in-home cancer treatment)

coder_notes: Health-services research trial of in-home vs clinic administration of patients' existing standard-of-care cancer therapy; glioblastoma is one of many eligible conditions (basket). No drug is investigational; the question is location of delivery, so no pharmacological candidate. The registered intervention is a generic 'Cancer Therapeutic Procedure'; the protocol lists ~23 eligible regimens (individual drugs not every patient receives), so one aggregate soc_backbone row is given rather than one row per listed drug. Treatment setting (newly diagnosed vs recurrent) not stated.
